title: Ribosome Preparation from Turquoise Killifish Skeletal Muscle for Cryo-EM
author: Lee, Kim
materials: This step describes preparing grids for cryo-EM. This step can be adjusted according to sample condition.28.Glow discharge both sides of a new grid with argon gas for 30 s which is the same condition above (step 27a).29.Coat the grid with graphene oxide. [Troubleshooting 4]a.Load 3 μL of graphene oxide solution onto the carbon side and incubate for 2 minb.Remove excess graphene oxide from the grid by touching the grid edge with filter paper and wash three times by placing the grid on distilled water drop.c.Remove excess water on the grid touching grid edge to filter paper.d.Dry for 5 min and use within a month without additional glow-discharge.Note: This step is performed according to a described protocol (Bokori-Brown et al., 2016).30.Cryo-EM grid preparationa.Set-up Vitrobot for Cryo-EM grid preparation.Note: We used VitrobotTM (FEI, Thermo Fisher Scientific) using the process parameters on the screen of the equipment.Blot time (s)3.0Blot force10Wait time (s)30.0Blot total1Drain time (s)0.0Skip applicationb.Load 3 μL of sample onto the graphene oxide coated grid.c.Wait 30 s and blot the ribosomes for 3 s with 10 of blotting force.Note: When you are trying to optimize sample blotting conditions for a new sample, it is recommended that 6–12 grids be prepared per sample and that different sample concentrations and waiting and blotting times to be tested.31.Store grids in liquid nitrogen before imaging and data collection.32.Collect data (Figure 3C).

steps.title: Anesthetize fish in tricaine
steps.instruction: Transfer 5–6‑week‑old turquoise killifish to 1.5 g L⁻¹ tricaine methanosulfonate solution and keep until gill movement stops completely.

steps.title: Remove skin and expose muscle
steps.instruction: Cut along the yellow lines shown in Figure 1 and peel off the skin to expose the underlying skeletal muscle.

steps.title: Collect skeletal muscle region
steps.instruction: Excise the muscle area outlined by the black line in Figure 1, taking care to avoid contamination with non‑muscle tissues.

steps.title: Freeze and store muscle tissue
steps.instruction: Immediately freeze the dissected muscle in liquid nitrogen and store at –80 °C until further processing.

steps.title: Grind frozen muscle to fine powder
steps.instruction: Grind the frozen muscle in liquid nitrogen with a mortar and pestle until particle size is < 100 µm (powder should adhere tightly to the mortar wall). If grinding 600 mg, continue for ~15 min. Note: bead‑beater with 3 mm–1 cm tungsten beads did not achieve the required fineness.

steps.title: Aliquot tissue powder and store
steps.instruction: Dispense 200 mg aliquots of the fine powder into e‑tubes and keep the tubes at –80 °C.

steps.title: Homogenize muscle in buffer
steps.instruction: Homogenize 600 mg of the finely ground skeletal muscle in 30 mL of homogenization buffer on ice.

steps.title: Filter homogenate through miracloth
steps.instruction: Pass the homogenate through two layers of miracloth, squeezing the cloth to recover as much liquid as possible and minimize sample loss.

steps.title: Centrifuge to remove debris
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the filtered homogenate at 14,000 × g for 5 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: High‑speed centrifugation of supernatant
steps.instruction: Transfer the supernatant to polypropylene centrifuge tubes and centrifuge at 30,000 × g for 20 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Repeat high‑speed centrifugation
steps.instruction: Again transfer the resulting supernatant to fresh tubes and repeat the 30,000 × g, 20 min, 4 °C spin.

steps.title: Collect cleared supernatant
steps.instruction: Collect the final clear supernatant in a 50 mL tube.

steps.title: Prepare sucrose cushion tubes
steps.instruction: Add 4 mL of sucrose cushion buffer to each ultra‑clear centrifuge tube; use a long‑tip Pasteur pipette as a funnel to fill from the bottom and avoid bubbles.

steps.title: Load supernatant onto sucrose cushion
steps.instruction: Gently layer the cleared supernatant from step 12 onto the sucrose cushion without disturbing the interface.

steps.title: Seal and ultracentrifuge tubes
steps.instruction: Balance the tubes, heat‑seal the tops with a seal former and cordless tube topper, then ultracentrifuge at 150,000 × g for 12 h at 4 °C.

steps.title: Remove supernatant and wash pellet
steps.instruction: Carefully discard the supernatant without losing the ribosome pellet, then wash the pellet three times with 1 mL washing buffer, letting the buffer flow over the surface and avoiding direct contact with the pellet.

steps.title: Verify ribosome pellet visibility
steps.instruction: Inspect the bottom of the tube for a transparent ribosome pellet.

steps.title: Resuspend pellet in resuspension buffer
steps.instruction: Collect the pellet with a diagonally cut pipette tip, transfer it to a new tube, and resuspend in 50 µL resuspension buffer. Remaining pellet can be recovered by adding buffer directly to the original tube.

steps.title: Gentle dissolution of ribosome pellet
steps.instruction: Pipette gently to dissolve the pellet, avoiding bubble formation.

steps.title: Final centrifugation and collect ribosome solution
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the suspension at 20,000 × g for 10 min at 4 °C and transfer the clear supernatant to a fresh tube; this contains the purified ribosomes.

steps.title: Glow discharge EM grids
steps.instruction: Place new grids in a glow‑discharge unit and expose both sides to argon gas for 30 s.

steps.title: Coat grids with graphene oxide
steps.instruction:
a) Load 3 µL graphene‑oxide solution onto the carbon side of the grid and incubate 2 min.
b) Remove excess by touching the grid edge with filter paper, then wash three times by placing the grid on a drop of distilled water.
c) Remove residual water by touching the edge to filter paper.
d) Air‑dry the grid for 5 min; use within one month without further glow‑discharge.

steps.title: Set Vitrobot parameters
steps.instruction: Program the Vitrobot (FEI, Thermo Fisher) with: blot time = 3.0 s, blot force = 10, wait time = 30.0 s, blot total = 1, drain time = 0.0 s, skip application.

steps.title: Apply sample and blot grid
steps.instruction: Load 3 µL of the ribosome sample onto the graphene‑oxide‑coated grid, wait 30 s, then blot for 3 s with blot force = 10.

steps.title: Store grids in liquid nitrogen
steps.instruction: Transfer the vitrified grids to liquid nitrogen for storage until imaging.

steps.title: Collect cryo‑EM data
steps.instruction: Load the stored grids into the cryo‑electron microscope and acquire data as described in Figure 3C.
